theme: I will tell of your name, lament turns to praise
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 22:22-31. Yesterday ended with a cry. Today the cry turns into praise. Read these verses aloud and notice who is included in the praise at the end.
settingTheScene: There is a break in Psalm 22 at verse 21. In Hebrew, the last words of that verse are something like “You have answered me.” The psalmist has been rescued. Everything after that point is a different kind of song. The man who was forsaken now tells others what God has done, and the song grows wider and wider until it takes in the whole earth and generations that have not yet been born.
observation: The psalmist says, “I will tell of your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will praise you” (v. 22).
He calls the congregation to praise: “You who fear the LORD, praise him!” (v. 23).
The reason: “For he has not despised or abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, and he has not hidden his face from him, but has heard, when he cried to him” (v. 24).
He vows to fulfill his vows in the presence of those who fear God (v. 25).
“The afflicted shall eat and be satisfied; those who seek him shall praise the LORD” (v. 26).
“All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the LORD, and all the families of the nations shall worship before you” (v. 27).
“Kingship belongs to the LORD, and he rules over the nations” (v. 28).
Even the dead are included: “All the prosperous of the earth eat and worship; before him shall bow all who go down to the dust” (v. 29).
The psalm ends with a future generation hearing about it: “that he has done it” (v. 31).
interpretation:
Look at what the sufferer does the moment he is rescued. He does not keep it private. “I will tell of your name to my brothers.” The rescue is a story, and a story is for telling. This is the way the Bible thinks of salvation: it is not only something that happens to a person. It becomes something the community knows and celebrates.

Verse 24 is worth stopping at. It is the answer to the first line of the psalm. Back in verse 1, God seemed to have forsaken the psalmist and hidden his face. Now he says, “He has not hidden his face from him.” What looked like abandonment turned out not to be. In the middle of the darkness, God was hearing. That does not mean that the suffering was unreal. But it means that the suffering was never the last word about God’s attitude.

The scope of the praise is dizzying. From one man in agony, we move to the congregation, then to the afflicted who eat and are satisfied, then to all the ends of the earth, then to all the families of the nations, and then to the dead and the unborn. One sufferer’s deliverance becomes the occasion for the worship of the whole world. This is the shape of the gospel. Through one man’s suffering and vindication, the nations are gathered.

That is why the New Testament reads Psalm 22 as the story of Jesus. Hebrews 2:12 puts verse 22 in Jesus’ mouth: “I will tell of your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will sing your praise.” The risen Jesus calls his people brothers, and he sings with them. The psalm that begins in the loneliest hour of history ends with a Savior who is surrounded by a people he has redeemed.

The last verse is also worth keeping. “They shall come and proclaim his righteousness to a people yet unborn, that he has done it.” Those words reach all the way to you.
connection: Hebrews 2:10-12 applies verse 22 to Jesus and his brothers. Revelation 7:9 pictures the fulfillment of verse 27: “a great multitude that no one could number, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages.” Jesus’ last words from the cross in John 19:30, “It is finished,” may echo the final words of Psalm 22:31, “that he has done it.”
application:
Tell someone this week what God has done for you. It does not need to be dramatic. Practice saying, “Let me tell you what the LORD did.”

Also think about the nations. Is there a mission or missionary you could pray for or give to in light of verse 27? Choose one.

If you are in a hard season, return to verse 24 and ask God to help you believe it before you see it.
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he has not hidden his face from you.
Ask him for words to tell what he has done.
Pray that he would gather people from every nation.
